items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: That's Basie's -- and Serge Chaloff and Buddy DeFranco. I couldn't see why he took any of them because Basie had enough soloists in his band to keep the thing going to me

ctx.x: I don't know. I don't know. That's what everybody wonders today, you know, why didn't he take myself? And -- like with Dicky Wells, the older guys out of the band. That's Basie's -- and Serge Chaloff and Buddy DeFranco. I couldn't see why he took any of them because Basie had enough soloists in his band to keep the thing going to me, you know.
Somebody must have sold him a bill of goods, you know. (Inaudible).

items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: Buddy DeFranco and Serge Chaloff. Well, Gus Johnson had been in the band before, in the old Basie band in Kansas City. But he had a bunch of guys that weren’t affiliated with Count Basie so far as the public was concerned at all. And he did get a lot of static at places that he played. Not that the guys that he had playing with him weren’t capable but they were just so used to seeing certain faces up there, like Buddy Tate…
Did you have any insight as to how he ended up choosing that or how it was put together for him?
